title: Operational readiness canvas and comms playbook for model serving reliability
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc defines an operational-readiness canvas and accompanying communications playbook for launching and operating model-serving endpoints under Redwood Inference’s reliability program. Focus: hosted API + dedicated capacity endpoints that run transformer-based text-generation models.

Goals (top-level):
- Clear, cross-functional readiness checklist so product, infra, SRE, and console teams sign off before canary/rollout.
- Explicit SLOs + measurement plan for the first 3 months post-launch.
- A repeatable comms cadence for incidents, rollouts, and SLO regressions.
- Runbook fragments and scheduled incident simulations (game days) to validate ops paths.

Audience:
- Primary: eng-sre, serving-runtime, infra, platform-engineering, product-hosted-api, developer-experience.
- Secondary: customer-success, security-and-compliance, solutions-engineering-and-professional-services.

Readiness canvas (checklist, to be ticked-off before canary):
1) Metrics & instrumentation (owner: Elena Garcia)
   - Metrics implemented and emitted: request_count, error_count, latency_p50/p90/p99, token_count, model_kv_cache_hit_rate.
   - Traces: distributed tracing enabled for request lifecycle (sample rate 10% initially).
   - Synthetic monitors: end-to-end generation monitor (happy-path prompt) every 1m.
   - Dashboard: baseline dashboard created and shared. Link: https://dashboards.redwood.company/d/model-serving/overview

2) SLOs & burn policies (owner: Maya Chen)
   - Latency SLO: p99 <= 250ms for short-chat path (<=64 tokens).
   - Availability SLO: successful_response_rate >= 99.5% (rolling 30d).
   - Error budget policy: automated throttling of non-critical bulk features when burn > 40% for > 6h.
   - Regression alert: if p99 increases 30% vs baseline for 15m, open an incident.

3) Observability & alerts (owner: Samir Patel)
   - Alert runbook linked to each metric alert.
   - Pager thresholds: p99 latency alert (pager when > 300ms for 5m), error_rate pager (when > 0.5% for 5m).
   - Alert noise reduction: group by route/model to avoid cross-noise.

4) Capacity & autoscaling (owner: Ravi Shah)
   - Load tests: baseline 1k concurrent inference requests sustained for 30m with acceptable error/latency.
   - Autoscale policy validated in staging with traffic replay.
   - Burst capacity plan: pre-warm GPU pool for high-volume customers with notification plumbing.

5) Failover & degradation modes (owner: Priya Nair)
   - Fallback model paths configured (quantized smaller model) and tested.
   - Graceful degradation UX: truncated responses + 503 hints to clients.

6) Security & compliance signoff (owner: security-and-compliance liaison)
   - KMS integration verified for private deployments.
   - Audit logging for inference requests enabled for sample customers.

7) Runbooks & playbooks (owner: eng-sre)
   - Incident triage runbook: how to map alerts -> severity -> response.
   - Post-incident action template included in runbook.

8) Customer comms & SLAs (owner: product-hosted-api)
   - Email and status-page templates written for incident and SLO burn notifications.
   - Customer success brief with escalation paths prepared.

Rollout plan (staging -> canary -> gradual ramp):
- Week 0: staging validation + chaos test (pod kill + network latency injection).
- Week 1: internal canary (10% internal traffic). Run for 48h, verify SLOs and no regressions.
- Week 2: 1% external canary (selected customers). Monitor 7d.
- Week 3-4: linear ramp 1% -> 10% -> 30% over 7d windows if SLOs hold.
- Gate: hold if cumulative error budget burn > 20% in any 24h window.

SLO measurement and reporting cadence:
- Daily: automated SLO report (rolling 7d) to SRE slack channel.
- Weekly: exec summary to product and infra leads (thresholds, burn rate, top contributors).
- Monthly: SLO review with customer success and solutions engineering (customer-visible impacts).

Comms playbook (templates and cadence):
- Pre-launch: kickoff email + readiness checklist to stakeholders + weekly sync.
- Canary start: notify channel + short status post with key metrics snapshot.
- Incident: three-tiered comms: (1) incident ack in #sre-ops (internal), (2) incident summary within 1h to affected product owners, (3) public status page update if customers impacted.
- SLO burn > 25%: scheduled async update + optional all-hands depending on scale.

Incident simulation schedule (game days):
- Monthly 2-hour tabletop with product + infra + SRE (first Friday of month).
- Quarterly full-blown simulated outage with traffic-shift exercise and oncall response.
- Post-sim retro within 48h with action owner assignments.

Risk register (high-level lines):
- Risk: KV cache warm-up causes p99 spikes during rollout. Mitigation: pre-warm caches, staggered ramp, synthetic cold-start tests. Owner: serving-runtime.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from overly-sensitive p50 alerts. Mitigation: tune alerting to p90/p99 and group by route. Owner: eng-sre.
- Risk: Model quantization causes quality regressions. Mitigation: gated A/B evals and small-sample human review. Owner: applied-ml.
- Risk: Network egress quota breach for bursty customers. Mitigation: burst throttle + billing alert + customer notice. Owner: infra.

Open questions (notes to self):
- How to reconcile token-based billing visibility with SLO dashboards (token spikes vs latency).
- Should we surface model-specific SLOs (e.g., long-context models) separately? Proposal: split SLOs per route/model family.
- Decide on synthetic monitor sampling cadence vs cost.

Tasks and immediate owners (next 30 days):
- Instrumentation PR merged (Elena) — due 2026-11-05.
- Create baseline load test scripts and run in staging (Ravi) — due 2026-11-12.
- Draft incident comms templates and status page examples (product-hosted-api, Priya) — due 2026-11-08.
- Define SLO reporting dashboard and automated report job (Samir) — due 2026-11-10.

Acceptance criteria for go/no-go to canary:
- All checkboxes in readiness canvas are green.
- No critical alerts firing in staging for 72h under replay traffic.
- Load test meets p99 <= 250ms and error rate <= 0.2% at target concurrency.
- Security audit signoff for KMS and logging.

Appendix: communication snippets
- Incident ack template: "We are aware of elevated error rates impacting model X. SRE is investigating — next update in 15 minutes. If you are experiencing production impact, please reply with examples and request prioritization."
- Canary start announcement: "Starting 1% external canary for model X at 2026-11-15T18:00Z. Watch #model-serving-canary for metrics; contact oncall if you see regressions."

Links and artifacts (reuse):
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/SRE/Model+Serving+SLOs
- Jira epic: SRE-1423
- Load test repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-loadtests

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize SLO wording and sign-off in cross-functional meeting (calendar invite: SLO-readiness-2026-11-02).
- Start synthetic monitor budget calculation and adjust cadence.
- Schedule first game day and invite product/infra leads.

-- end of working draft --

Notes: this doc is deliberately operational and pragmatic — keep short checklists and explicit owners. Will expand with specific runbook links once PRs land.
